responses.leak_example: days_past_due_90 is a leaked field because it is only available after the application. Using it at application time would give the model information about the later outcome that would not be available when a real credit decision is made.
responses.split_reason: The validation uses forward time ordering, customer separation, anda strict 90-day maturity rule so that each validation period represents later applications and its training data contains only labels that would have matured by the validation start. Customer separation also prevents the same customer's information from appearing in both training and validation. In this run, all three forward folds had zero shared customers.
responses.observed_gap: The leaky random control produced mean ROC-AUC 0.9999 and mean AP 0.9988, compared with ROC-AUC 0.8010 and AP 0.3110 for the clean random control. The observed AP gap between the leaky and clean random controls was 0.6879. This very large increase shows how leakage can create unrealistically strong apparent model performance. The honest fixed protocol produced mean ROC-AUC 0.7976 and AP 0.3153, while the honest reserved-search protocol produced ROC-AUC 0.7855 and AP 0.3133.
responses.imputer_reason: Imputation must be learned only from the training data within each fold. If imputation values were calculated using validation data, information about the later validation population would influence preprocessing and leak into model development.
responses.limitations: The results do not prove that any protocol or model is universally superior. The time-based protocols evaluate 5,039 later eligible applications and use different training sizes, so their results are not directly interchangeable with the random controls covering 10,000 requests. The reported variation across three folds is descriptive rather than a confidence interval. The reserved tuning cohort is also relatively small: 1,935 applications with 176 positives, which limits the hyperparameter search. Finally, the out-of-fold predictions are not an independent final test and do not establish calibration, fairness, or future production performance.
